methods.label: Test cancellation prime by prime
methods.sourceMethod: The prime-cancellation arguments in the LIVE reference and AoPS Solutions 1 and 2, together with the supplied harmonic-number lemma. The criterion is justified here by clearing denominators, using congruence only modulo p.

annotationRationale: The main challenge is recognizing when prime factors cancel from the least common denominator. The alternative supplies a complete arithmetic route without modular reasoning; recurrence concepts remain local to that method.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Cancellation occurs exactly for n=6,7,8,18,19,20,21,22, giving 8 and choice D. The statement, choices and key agree. No figure contradiction is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: No shared-bank methods were supplied. The LIVE recurrence is retained as exact-fraction-recurrence. AoPS Solutions 1 and 2 and the harmonic-number lemma are combined into prime-cancellation. These provide two independently complete routes; no additional route is needed.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed prime-factorization, congruence, LCM and fraction-reduction concepts describe the main route accurately. GCF and unlike-denominator addition appropriately support the question. Keeping recurrence local to the arithmetic alternative is reasonable.
review.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: For q=p^a maximal, only denominators jq survive modulo p, with j≤t<p. Since j is coprime to q and divides L_n, it divides B=L_n/q. Thus the reduced harmonic numerator gives the stated cancellation test. The harmonic values and all prime-table cases are correct: p=3 contributes eight values, and p=5 contributes only three already included. The n=1 endpoint is handled.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The cited LIVE and AoPS material supports the claimed argument. The candidate correctly works only modulo p, avoiding the unjustified modulo-p^e assertion in AoPS Solution 1. Its explanatory development is original and correctly labeled source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why cancellation is the right target. Clearing denominators makes the unfamiliar harmonic-number criterion accessible without modular inverses. The two tables and interval examples sufficiently justify the exhaustive count.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All four immediate IDs fit: prime exponents determine surviving terms, congruence discards divisible terms, LCM supplies the denominator, and fraction reduction identifies cancellation. No additional node is needed for the derived harmonic criterion.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native LCM and fraction-reduction topic links apply. Prime-exponent and congruence reasoning extends beyond these elementary topics and has no supplied CN alignment.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: The supplied partial 6.NS.B.4 LCM link gives limited overlap; the many-number LCM and cancellation argument exceed its bounds and do not cover its distributive component. The central competition concepts have no supplied US links.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: The immediate concepts precisely cover the argument, and the elementary supporting concepts adequately ground the derived criterion.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Both recurrences follow by expressing the previous sum and 1/n over L_n. All 22 LCM and numerator entries are correct. The nonunit gcds are 3 at n=6,7,8,18,19; 15 at n=20; and 45 at n=21,22. Every other gcd is 1, so the independent arithmetic count is 8.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The LIVE reference explicitly supplies recursive accumulation and the same cancellation ratios. The candidate develops that idea into an independently checkable integer table, with correct attribution and source-informed-original classification.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The recurrence, starting values and worked n=6 calculation explain how to reconstruct the table. The large entries are arithmetic work, but no mathematical transition or case is omitted.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: Simple recurrence, unlike-denominator addition, LCM, fraction reduction and GCF are all directly used. No modular-arithmetic or prime-factorization node is needed for this route.
